site.title: Tempura — free focus timer for Pomodoro, 52/17 and Flowtime
site.description: Free, open-source focus timer for Linux, Windows and macOS. Eight rhythms — {{rhythms}} — or your own. Local-first: no account, no cloud.
site.ogDescription: A focus timer with eight rhythms, not one. Free for Linux, Windows and macOS — local-first, no account.
site.deck: {{rhythms}} — or your own. Pick the rhythm that fits the work. Tempura keeps time from the tray, entirely on your machine: no account, no cloud.

site.timerAlt: Tempura timer on Sprint: 6:20 remaining, working on Learning Tauri
site.techniqueNote: Work rhythms for the desk — not a diagnosis, and not medical advice.
site.pointClockBody: The countdown belongs to the native side, so a hidden window or a machine that slept does not cheat the session. Start, pause, skip, reset, stop — the tray tooltip stays live.
site.pointTrayBody: Tempura lives in the system tray. Closing the window hides it; quitting is a deliberate choice from the tray or Settings. Launch at login if you want it waiting with the kettle.
site.pointLocalBody: Presets, settings, and history sit in local SQLite under the app data directory. No accounts, no cloud, no sync — MIT licensed, yours to inspect.
site.installLinux: AppImage: chmod +x the file, then run it. Debian: install the .deb. Fedora and openSUSE: the .rpm. You may need FUSE for AppImage.
site.installWindows: SmartScreen may warn on the first run — the build is unsigned. More info → Run anyway, or use the MSI.
site.installMacos: Gatekeeper may block an unsigned app. Right-click the app → Open. Apple Silicon and Intel each have their own disk image.
site.rhythmsIntro: One interval is not for everyone. Eight rhythms come in the box, each drawn here as one full set of focus and breaks. Switch between them from the timer in a click.
site.featuresHeading: Made for the work, not the timer
site.statsBody: Pick any day, week, month, year or all time and compare it with the period before. A clear picture, not a guilt trip.
site.statsPoint1: When you focus best, on a weekday × hour map
site.statsPoint2: Which rhythm suits you: the ones you actually finish
site.statsPoint3: What the hours went to, task by task
site.statsPoint4: Today, hour by hour, right under the timer
site.statsPoint5: Export to CSV or JSON whenever you like
site.statsAlt: Tempura Stats: a week of focus with totals and a weekday × hour map of when you focus
site.featKeysBody: Space starts and pauses, S skips, Esc hides. Optional global shortcuts work from any app, and a screen reader announces every phase.
site.featNotifyBody: A notification when each phase ends, an optional soft sound, and a halfway tick if you like to know where you are.
site.featThemesBody: {{themes}}: palettes with checked contrast, for bright mornings and late nights.
site.featLangBody: 15 languages, with right-to-left layouts for Arabic and Hebrew. The clock reads the same either way.
site.privacyUpdates: Its only call out is an update check against GitHub Releases at launch. No telemetry, and you can switch it off.
site.faqFreeA: Yes. Tempura is open source under the MIT license: no trial, no subscription, no ads. The code is on GitHub.
site.faqAccountQ: Do I need an account or an internet connection?
site.faqAccountA: No to both. There is nothing to sign up for, and your techniques, settings and history live in a local database on your computer.
site.faqPomodoroQ: How is it different from a Pomodoro timer?
site.faqPomodoroA: {{classic}} 25/5 is in the box, but it is one rhythm of eight. {{sprint}}, {{deep}}, {{fiftyTwo}} and {{ultradian}} set other fixed intervals; {{flowtime}} counts up and sizes the break to the work; {{hybrid}} starts fixed and can roll into {{flowtime}}. Or bake your own.
site.faqWhichQ: Which technique should I start with?
site.faqWhichA: {{sprint}} gets you moving on something hard, {{classic}} suits lighter tasks, and {{fiftyTwo}} or {{deep}} fit long stretches once you are in. Stats show which rhythms you actually finish, so the numbers can decide.
site.faqWarnQ: Why do Windows or macOS warn me when I open it?
site.faqWarnA: The builds are not signed with a paid certificate yet. Each one is built by GitHub Actions from the public source, and its SHA-256 checksum is listed on this page and in the release.
site.faqUpdateA: At launch Tempura asks GitHub whether a newer version exists; you can turn that off in {{about}}. Updates are signed, and nothing installs until you choose “{{update}}”.
site.faqMobileA: Not yet. Tempura is built for the computer you work at: Linux, Windows and macOS.
site.finalBody: Free for Linux, Windows and macOS. No sign-up, nothing to set up first.
